cues.en: Another issue you'll deal with in the real world is that it's easy to offend people, without ever intending to do so.
cues.zh: 在真實世界還會遇到另一個問題：你很容易在無意之間冒犯別人。

cues.en: I don't know what sort of creature this is, but he looks offended and you better hope your recommender system isn't what offended him.
cues.zh: 我不知道這是什麼生物，但它看起來被冒犯了。你最好希望不是你的推薦系統惹惱它。

cues.en: Let's go back to the year 2006, when Walmart's website was starting to experiment with making recommendations.
cues.zh: 回到 2006 年，當時 Walmart 網站剛開始嘗試做推薦。

cues.en: As part of a manual rule someone added into it to promote DVDs about the black civil rights leader Martin Luther King, their recommendations started to pair movies about Martin Luther King
cues.zh: 有人為了推廣黑人公民權領袖 Martin Luther King 的 DVD，手動加入一條規則，導致推薦開始把 Martin Luther King 的電影，

cues.en: with a lot of different things including, unfortunately, movies such as Planet of the Apes and Charlie and the Chocolate Factory.
cues.zh: 與各種不同內容配對，其中不幸包括 Planet of the Apes 和 Charlie and the Chocolate Factory 等電影。

cues.en: You can imagine that people being told they might enjoy a movie about Martin Luther King because they liked Planet of the Apes didn't go over very well.
cues.zh: 你可以想像，因為喜歡 Planet of the Apes，就被告知可能喜歡 Martin Luther King 的電影，人們不會有好反應。

cues.en: And you'd be right, the story got picked up by national news, Walmart had to issue an apology and donate money to civil rights causes, and they scrapped their entire recommendation system.
cues.zh: 確實如此。這件事登上全國新聞，Walmart 必須道歉並捐款支持公民權議題，還廢除了整個推薦系統。

cues.en: Presumably, people lost their jobs due to this.
cues.zh: 想必有人因此失去工作。

cues.en: There are some topics that are just too touchy for you to deal with, and that's where stoplists come in.
cues.zh: 有些主題太敏感，不適合碰，這就是排除清單派上用場的地方。

cues.en: There are certain terms and keywords where if they are present in the titles, descriptions, or categories of the items in your catalog, your recommender system shouldn't even know that they exist.
cues.zh: 有些詞彙與關鍵字，如果出現在商品目錄項目的標題、說明或類別裡，推薦系統根本就不應該知道這些項目存在。

cues.en: If titles associated with race were omitted from the training of Walmart's recommender system entirely, then they would have no potential to cause offensive pairings with other items.
cues.zh: 如果 Walmart 的推薦系統訓練時，完全排除與種族相關的作品，就不會有機會與其他項目形成冒犯性的配對。

cues.en: That's all a stoplist is, checking to see if an item might cause unwanted controversy before you let it into your recommender system.
cues.zh: 排除清單就是如此：在項目進入推薦系統前，檢查它是否可能引起不必要的爭議。

cues.en: There are a lot of topics that might cause a crisis if they are paired with the wrong items, and it's best to err on the side of caution.
cues.zh: 許多主題若搭配錯誤項目，都可能引發危機，最好謹慎一點。

cues.en: I don't care what your own moral or political beliefs are, if you're working for a business, you have a responsibility to uphold the reputation of that business.
cues.zh: 我不在乎你自己的道德或政治信念。如果為企業工作，你就有責任維護企業的聲譽。

cues.en: If you don't agree with your customers' beliefs, frankly that doesn't matter.
cues.zh: 如果不同意顧客的信念，坦白說，那並不重要。

cues.en: You don't want your recommender system to end up on the front page of the New York Times, and to be dragged in front of the CEO of your company to explain why you recommended Adolf Hitler's memoirs
cues.zh: 你不會希望推薦系統登上 New York Times 頭版，還被叫到執行長面前，解釋為何把 Adolf Hitler 的回憶錄，

cues.en: to someone looking for books about their favorite politician.
cues.zh: 推薦給正在找自己喜愛政治人物相關書籍的人。

cues.en: Some things are no-brainers.
cues.zh: 有些情況很明顯。

cues.en: Content that's about sex is best avoided, you don't want to end up recommending sex toys alongside children's books, for example.
cues.zh: 最好避免性相關內容，例如你不會希望在童書旁推薦情趣用品。

cues.en: Items with vulgarity in their titles or descriptions will set a lot of people off.
cues.zh: 標題或說明包含粗俗用語的項目，會惹惱很多人。

cues.en: Some topics are even illegal in certain countries, such as Nazism in Germany and really, recommending Nazi content probably isn't a good idea anywhere.
cues.zh: 有些主題在某些國家甚至違法，例如德國的納粹主義。而且說真的，無論在哪裡推薦納粹內容，大概都不是好主意。

cues.en: But many countries also ban explicit lists of political terms that you are required to honor if you're doing business there.
cues.zh: 但許多國家也明文禁止一系列政治詞彙，在當地做生意就必須遵守。

cues.en: If you want to do business in China for example, you're going to need to stoplist items that contain topics the Chinese government doesn't like.
cues.zh: 例如，如果想在中國做生意，就需要把含有中國政府不喜歡主題的項目加入排除清單。

cues.en: Terrorism and political extremism will certainly tick some customers off, as will religious topics, especially more fundamentalist religions.
cues.zh: 恐怖主義與政治極端主義肯定會惹惱一些顧客，宗教主題也一樣，尤其是較基本教義派的宗教。

cues.en: It's not about making value judgements, it's just the universal adage that you shouldn't talk about politics or religion with strangers.
cues.zh: 這不是要做價值判斷，只是那句普遍的忠告：別與陌生人談政治或宗教。

cues.en: Some things are more subtle, however.
cues.zh: 不過，有些情況更微妙。

cues.en: Items associated with bereavement or medical care comes to mind.
cues.zh: 例如與喪親或醫療照護相關的項目。

cues.en: Imagine you're caring for a loved one who is suffering from terminal cancer, and you bought some books about cancer.
cues.zh: 想像你正在照顧罹患癌症末期的摯愛，並買了一些癌症相關書籍。

cues.en: Once that loved one passes away, you certainly don't want to be reminded of it be seeing recommendations for more books about cancer every time you come back to a website.
cues.zh: 摯愛過世後，你當然不希望每次回到網站，都看見更多癌症書籍推薦，提醒你這件事。

cues.en: It's best to just leave books like that out of your training entirely.
cues.zh: 最好直接把這類書籍完全排除於訓練資料之外。

cues.en: Or maybe you're recommending baby diapers to people who bought the book What to Expect When You're Expecting.
cues.zh: 或者，你向買過 What to Expect When You're Expecting 的人推薦嬰兒尿布。

cues.en: Seems reasonable at first, but would you want to see recommendations for diapers if your pregnancy actually ended in a tragic miscarriage?
cues.zh: 乍看很合理，但如果懷孕最後不幸流產，你還會想看到尿布推薦嗎？

cues.en: Perhaps books about prenatal care are best stoplisted as well.
cues.zh: 或許產前照護書籍，也最好加入排除清單。

cues.en: Sometimes, stoplists might be used for other purposes entirely.
cues.zh: 有時排除清單的用途完全不同。

cues.en: Perhaps you don't want to promote certain items due to business concerns, because they compete with items you sell yourself.
cues.zh: 也許出於商業考量，你不想推廣某些項目，因為它們與你自家販售的產品競爭。

cues.en: As much as you might want your recommender system to be a completely neutral, level playing field, that's just not the reality of business.
cues.zh: 即使很希望推薦系統完全中立、公平，商業現實也不是如此。

cues.en: There may be items you don't want to recommend strictly for business reasons and nothing more.
cues.zh: 可能有些項目，純粹因為商業理由而不想推薦，僅此而已。

cues.en: You can't anticipate every PR disaster though, so it's important that your stoplist can be updated and applied quickly should the need arise.
cues.zh: 不過，你無法預料每一場公關災難，因此重要的是，必要時能迅速更新並套用排除清單。

cues.en: You might even have an emergency stoplist that prevents titles from being displayed on the front end, while the stoplist on your backend training system has time to work its way through.
cues.zh: 你甚至可以有一份緊急排除清單，阻止作品在前端顯示，讓後端訓練系統的排除清單有時間逐步生效。

cues.en: Not every offensive recommendation pairing is an accident, either.
cues.zh: 而且，不是每個冒犯性的推薦配對都是意外。

cues.en: If you are using implicit ratings information, for example user clicks or search terms, it's possible for people to game your recommender system and generate fake associations between items
cues.zh: 如果使用隱含評分資訊，例如點擊或搜尋詞，就可能有人操弄推薦系統，在項目之間建立虛假的關聯，

cues.en: by simulating enough traffic on your website to create those associations.
cues.zh: 透過模擬網站上足夠多的流量，製造這些關聯。

cues.en: For example, right now if I do a Google image search for the word idiot, pictures of the current US President will appear due to a coordinated campaign from his opponents.
cues.zh: 例如，在我錄課的此刻，如果在 Google 圖片搜尋輸入 idiot，會出現當時美國總統的照片，這是他的反對者協同行動造成的。

cues.en: Part of the role of your stoplist is to have a quick way to respond to attacks like that, because even though half of Google's customers might find that amusing, they're risking a boycott from the other half who do not.
cues.zh: 排除清單的用途之一，就是能迅速回應這類攻擊。因為即使一半的 Google 顧客覺得有趣，他們也冒著被另一半不覺得有趣的人抵制的風險。
